mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of quarters following YoY GDP acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, it signals a weakening labor market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 0.5pp+ rise in UNRATE over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls turns negative, it signals a potential recession that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters following a YoY decline in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate is rising, it signals a weakening economy that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST declines > 10% YoY and UNRATE is rising.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth accelerates by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a strong economic expansion that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of quarters where INDPRO growth > 2% QoQ and FEDFUNDS < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPI) rises by more than 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate is above 3%, it signals a high-inflation environment that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of months where CPI YoY > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive and accelerating, and the unemployment rate is below 5%, it signals a strong and stable economic expansion that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of quarters where GDPC1 growth is positive and accelerating, and UNRATE < 5%.
